result.note: Tests the funding body, its parent department, the RDI Fund and the cost share for Project VeerAI's AI surveillance chip.

questions.prompt: In October 2026, the Centre agreed to fund Project VeerAI, an AI chip for CCTV systems developed by Bengaluru-based BigEndian Semiconductors. Consider the following statements:
items: The Technology Development Board, which is providing the funding, is part of the Department of Science and Technology.
The government funding covers the entire cost of Project VeerAI.
The money comes from the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the INR 1.3 billion covers only half of Project VeerAI's INR 2.6 billion cost. The funding aims to take the camera-focused chip from mid-stage testing to a deployment-ready product, sold first to surveillance buyers in India and the Global South.
questions.source: The Technology Development Board (TDB), part of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), signed an agreement on Monday to give Bengaluru-based BigEndian Semiconductors INR 1.3 billion (USD 13.5 million) from the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.
